alignment.strategy: Both VV bands and binary masks are evaluated on the exact before-VV CRS and affine transform; explicit nearest-neighbor reprojection, no smoothing.
alignment.caveat: Grid alignment is not measured subpixel co-registration, independent 10 m spatial accuracy or radiometric equivalence.

computation.domain: Stored COPERNICUS/S1_GRD decibels; no linear-power averaging or ratio conversion.
computation.change: later_dB - before_dB on common valid pixels; a log-ratio display, not a flood classifier.
computation.masks: Original VV data masks > 0, nearest-neighbor aligned; common mask is their intersection clipped to the original AOI. No intensity threshold, speckle filter or flood/permanent-water mask is applied.
computation.areaDenominator: Valid-pixel percentages use AOI raster pixel area on the common grid; vector-AOI percentages are also reported. Footprint percentages use vector AOI area. Vector geometry and raster pixel-area calculation/discretization differ; neither denominator is silently substituted.
computation.statisticsSupport: All VV and change statistics use the same common valid pixel support; angle statistics additionally require both angle masks. Percentiles are EE reducer estimates.

caveats: Sentinel-1A versus Sentinel-1B radiometric equivalence has not been validated.
Compare incidence-angle distributions and stable targets before interpreting change.
Speckle, wet soil, land cover, urban geometry and acquisition differences can alter backscatter.
Masks establish available samples, not that every sample is free of border noise or other artifacts.
Single-scene overlap omits part of the AOI; no AOI-wide flood-area claim is supported.

quality.limitation: Research prototype: May 30 follows the documented event peak. Residual water is unverified. These are backscatter observations and exploratory radar change, not confirmed flood extent, depth, classification or detection accuracy.

reasons: Orbit direction, relative orbit, instrument mode and resolution match.
Both scene footprints cover at least 90% of the study area.
Preferred IW configuration with shared VV is available.
Verified joint footprint covers 92.91404030186871% of the study area (minimum 90%).
pairAssessment.meaning: Metadata/pixel comparison only; flood conditions are not established.

methodology.name: AHP-Weighted GIS Multi-Criteria Analysis
methodology.weightStatus: Demonstration AHP judgments - Not literature validated

ahp.excludes: WorldCover class 80 and original factor/index no-data masks
ahp.evaluation: Existing AHP image evaluated on analysisProjection.atScale(30), then nearest-neighbor sampled onto the exact before-VV grid.

yearly-conservative-v1.inference: Only observed annual classes 1, 2 and 3 support analysis; all other states remain unknown.
yearly-conservative-v1.processingCaveat: No post-cutoff image entries are used. JRC v1.4 is a retrospective processed archive, not a product claimed to have been available contemporaneously in 2017.
yearly-conservative-v1.seasonalWater: Annual class 2 remains separately identified and potentially eligible; seasonal refilling can be a false candidate.

yearly-monthly-dry-v1.inference: Only unknown annual pixels with >=3 observed monthly class-1 detections and zero observed monthly class-2 detections gain inferred eligibility. This is historical non-water evidence, not proof of event-date dry land or absence of permanent water.
yearly-monthly-dry-v1.processingCaveat: No post-cutoff image entries are used. JRC v1.4 is a retrospective processed archive, not a product claimed to have been available contemporaneously in 2017.
yearly-monthly-dry-v1.seasonalWater: Annual class 2 remains separately identified and potentially eligible; seasonal refilling can be a false candidate.

methodology.area: ee.Image.pixelArea(), weighted sum within original AOI, exact before-VV Projection including affine origin; no bestEffort, scale override, or pixel-count area approximation.

methodology.commonDomain: AOI AND AHP land-class mask AND recognized codes 1..4 AND actual before/later VV support AND complete 30 m smoothing neighborhoods AND actual smoothed value masks AND historical supported/eligible non-permanent water domain AND known terrain.
methodology.stageDomain: Raw, terrain and final use the identical domain for each reference method. Known steep pixels remain supported filter rejections; missing terrain is excluded at all stages.
methodology.referenceDomain: Reference-specific denominators are reported separately; identical-cross-reference results use their intersection for all stages. Connectivity is computed by the existing graph on original SAR support before restricting measurement to AHP/common domains.
methodology.noData: Only validity masks are filled false for set operations. Candidate transparency is filled false exclusively inside an independently established supported domain.
methodology.diagnostics: Exclusive loss ledger partitions raster AOI in listed order. Marginal areas overlap and must not be summed.
methodology.statisticalInference: None; no independent ground truth or significance tests.

caveats: This is preliminary spatial agreement, not independent validation. No independent event flood labels are used.
AHP susceptibility and event-date experimental SAR responses represent different concepts. Supported non-candidates are not confirmed dry or flood-free.
Sentinel-1 May 30 observations are after the approximate May 2017 event peak; peak inundation cannot be inferred.
The pair uses Sentinel-1A and Sentinel-1B; cross-platform consistency and subpixel co-registration have not been independently verified.

Historical JRC water support has major limitations: sparse annual observations, seasonal water eligibility, retrospective processing, and optional monthly non-water inference do not establish event-date land or water.

AHP uses demonstration judgments and preliminary class cutoffs. WorldCover 2021 and historical global water occurrence are not contemporaneous 2017 inputs; this is retrospective susceptibility comparison.
The 10 m evaluation grid does not create independent 10 m measurements from 30 m SRTM/JRC inputs. Spatially dependent pixels provide no significance or causal evidence.
Slope and connected-component screening can remove real flood responses. Agreement changes or expanded support do not imply improved accuracy.
Neither function currently establishes verified flood prediction accuracy.
